props.title: Ishq

sections.content: Ishq (1997) represents a pivotal moment in 90s Bollywood romantic comedies, blending slapstick humor with intense emotional drama. Director Indra Kumar, fresh off the success of Dil (1990), crafted a tale of cross-class romance that became a template for later films. The film pairs Aamir Khan and Ajay Devgn at their comedic peaks, while Juhi Chawla and Kajol deliver powerhouse performances that balance the broader comedy with genuine pathos. The film's massive commercial success influenced a wave of similar rich-poor romance narratives like Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998) and Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999).

sections.content: The film's treatment of class conflict through comedy marks a significant shift from the angry young man narratives of the 70s and 80s. Where films like Deewaar (1975) approached class warfare through violence and drama, Ishq uses humor to disarm these tensions. The famous scene where Ajay Devgn and Aamir Khan dangle from a high-rise building became a cultural touchstone, demonstrating how the film balanced nerve-wracking thrills with comedy.

Musically, Ishq showcases Anu Malik at his peak, with "Mr. Lova Lova" becoming a defining song of the era. The film's soundtrack follows the template set by Rangeela (1995) in incorporating Western pop elements while maintaining traditional Indian melodic structures. This fusion approach influenced countless films including Dil To Pagal Hai (1997) and Yes Boss (1997). SUBHEAD: Impact on 90s Romance Cinema

sections.content: The success of Ishq cemented several tropes that dominated late 90s Bollywood: the rich-poor romance, comedy as social commentary, and the two-couple narrative structure. Films like Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999) and Taal (1999) followed this template while adding their own artistic flourishes. The film's influence extends to modern rom-coms like 2 States (2014), which continue to explore class differences through humor rather than melodrama.
